chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Ubaydah, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'A woman is not married off simultaneously with her paternal aunt, nor with her maternal aunt, nor with her milk-sister.'

And he said: 'Indeed, Ali (peace be upon him) mentioned to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) the daughter of Hamzah, so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Do you not know that she is the daughter of your brother from suckling?' And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and his uncle Hamzah (may Allah be pleased with him) had both suckled from one woman.'
ai.seo_question: What are the prohibitions regarding simultaneous marriage to female relatives and milk-sisters in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* codifies the prohibition of simultaneous marriage to close female relatives, extending the concept of *radha'* (milk kinship) to include paternal and maternal aunts. It highlights the scholarly consensus on the legal equivalence of milk-siblings to blood-siblings by citing the Prophet’s confirmation that Hamzah’s daughter was Ali’s milk-sister, as both had suckled from the same woman. This incident underscores the practical application of milk kinship in determining marital eligibility within Shia jurisprudence.
